ety.text: From Middle English it, hit ( > dialectal English hit (“it”)), from Old English hit (“it”), from Proto-West Germanic *hit, from Proto-Germanic *hit (“this, this one”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱe (“here; here”). Cognates Cognate with Yola it, t', yt (“it”), North Frisian at, et, 't (“it”), Saterland Frisian et (“it”), West Frisian it (“it”), Dutch het (“it”), Luxembourgish hatt (“her, it, she”), Elfdalian eð (“it”); also Primitive Irish ᚕᚑᚔ (koi, “here”), Latin cis (“short of; before”), hic (“this”), Greek εκείνος (ekeínos, “that; those”).

senses.d: The third-person singular neuter personal pronoun used to refer to an inanimate object, abstract entity, or non-human living thing.
ex: Take this book and put it on the shelf.
Take each day as it comes.

senses.d: A third-person singular personal pronoun used to refer to a baby or child, especially of unknown gender.
ex: She took the baby and held it in her arms.
The sky was dripping. Like a tap that a child has tried its hardest to turn off but hasn't quite managed.

senses.d: A third-person singular pronoun used to refer to an unspecified person.
ex: She had never seen that each human being was different, would react differently, had its own peculiar idiosyncrasies.

senses.d: An affectionate third-person singular personal pronoun.
A third-person singular personal pronoun used to refer to an animate referent who is transgender or non-binary.
Refers to someone being identified, often on the phone, but not limited to this situation.
ex: It's me, John.
Somebody wanted a drink, didn't they? Who was it?

senses.d: The impersonal pronoun, used without referent as the subject of an impersonal verb or statement (known as the dummy pronoun, dummy it or weather it).
ex: It is nearly 10 o’clock.

senses.d: The impersonal pronoun, used without referent, or with unstated but contextually implied referent, in various short idioms or expressions.
ex: rough it
live it up

senses.d: Referring to a desirable quality or ability, or quality of being successful, fashionable or in vogue.
ex: After all these years, she still has it.

senses.d: Referring to sexual intercourse or other sexual activity.
ex: I caught them doing it.
Are you getting it regularly?

senses.d: One who is neither a he nor a she; a creature; a dehumanized being.
ex: Too often, children become an "it" in their homes and their humanness is devalued.

senses.d: The person who chases and tries to catch the other players in the playground game of tag.
ex: In the next game, Adam and Tom will be it…
Tag, you're it!
Let's play it at breaktime.

senses.d: A desirable characteristic, as being fashionable.
ex: Man, he's really got it.
She's the it girl, at least for this Fall.
Bro, that shirt is not it.
OMG, they were doing it in the storage room.
She really has it going on.

senses.d: Most fashionable, popular, or in vogue.
ex: Going away for the weekend and feel the need to profile en route? This is the "it" bag.
With Hit Girl, Moretz is this year's It Girl, alternately sweet, savage and scary.
